AXP.rationale: AXP presents a moderately attractive case anchored by accelerating revenue (+9.3% YoY) and EPS growth (+17.6% YoY) with elite margins (26.6% net margin) and ROE (33.0%), while the P/E at 20.94x sits in the lower quartile of its 365-day range (18.4x–25.3x), implying the market is paying less for improved earnings power. The franchise is durable: closed-loop model, $10B in record net card fees (up 18% YoY), 20 consecutive quarters of international billings growth, and demonstrated pricing power via the $895 Platinum fee reset. Berkshire's ~22% stake reinforces long-term confidence. However, the score is capped below +0.5 by two real concerns: (1) operating cash flow fell -20.2% YoY to $3.80B despite record earnings, creating a quality-of-earnings divergence, and (2) debt-to-equity has expanded to 1.73x (upper bound of range) as the balance sheet grows faster than equity. Competitive pressure from Capital One/Discover and Chase Sapphire Reserve is structural and intensifying. The Q2 2026 earnings report (July 24) provides a near-term catalyst — consensus expects $4.39 EPS (+7.6% YoY) — but this is a confirmation event rather than a re-rating trigger, warranting only a modest pillar-3 bump. On balance, a sound franchise at a reasonable-to-cheap valuation with manageable but real headwinds.
